stories.headline: Canadian poet Anne Carson wins the Nobel Prize in Literature
stories.summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature has gone to the Canadian poet Anne Carson. The Swedish Academy named the 76-year-old on 8 October, praising a bold and inventive body of work that moves between poetry, translations of ancient Greek and collaborations with dancers and musicians. Carson is the third Canadian-born writer to take the prize.

stories.headline: British wildlife will replace people on Bank of England notes
stories.summary: The Bank of England has announced what will appear on its next set of pound sterling notes. An Atlantic puffin, a barn owl, a buff-tailed bumblebee and a European hedgehog have been chosen. It is the first time animals have replaced people on banknotes in England, a change intended to increase awareness of British wildlife.

stories.headline: Teruaki Satō takes Japanese baseball's Triple Crown
stories.summary: Teruaki Satō of the Hanshin Tigers has won the Triple Crown in Japanese baseball. The feat goes to a player who leads a league in batting average, home runs and runs batted in over the same season. The last NPB player to manage it was Munetaka Murakami in 2022.

stories.headline: A golden coral off Costa Rica needs a family of its own
stories.summary: A bright yellow coral found on underwater mountains off Costa Rica belongs to no known coral family, so scientists have created a new one for it. Its new genus name, Laurinque, means golden tree in Quenya, the Elvish language created by J.R.R. Tolkien. The branching colonies were found between 360 and 529 metres below the surface of the Pacific.

sources.excerpt: Anne Carson has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature for her genre-bending works that range from poetry and ancient Greek translations to collaborations with dancers and musicians.

The Swedish Academy recognized the 76-year-old Canadian poet, essayist and translator on October 8 for "her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature."
Carson is the third Canadian-born writer to win the literature prize, following Saul Bellow in 1976 and Alice Munro in 2013.
The Bank of England announces that the Atlantic puffin, barn owl, buff-tailed bumblebee, and European hedgehog will feature on the next set of pound sterling notes to be issued in the United Kingdom.
It will be the first time animals have replaced people on banknotes in England, which is intended to increase awareness of British wildlife.
In baseball, Teruaki Satō of the Hanshin Tigers wins the Triple Crown; the last NPB Triple Crown was won by Munetaka Murakami in 2022.
The term "Triple Crown" generally refers to the batting achievement of leading a league in batting average, home runs, and runs batted in (RBI) over the same season.
Teruaki Satō is a Japanese professional baseball infielder for the Hanshin Tigers of Nippon Professional Baseball (NPB).
Scientists surveying underwater mountains off Costa Rica have identified a remarkable new coral that is unlike any known coral family.
The bright yellow coral, which has a branching, tree-like appearance, was discovered between 360 and 529 meters below the Pacific Ocean's surface.
The new genus, Laurinque, is derived from "Laurinquë," which means "golden tree" in Quenya, the Elvish language created by J.R.R. Tolkien for The Lord of the Rings and The Silmarillion.
